newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-GILLINGHAM ADDED TO TRI-NATIONS SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GILLINGHAM ADDED TO TRI-NATIONS SQUAD.

text.p: Uncapped centre Joe Gillingham was added to the Springbok Tri-Nations squad on Monday for Saturday's match against New Zealand in Auckland.

The Gauteng Lions player was called in to replace the injured Danie van Schalkwyk of Northern Transvaal, who broke his left ankle during South Africa's 32-20 loss against Australia in Brisbane on Saturday.
Gillingham will link up with the squad in Auckland on Thursday, Springbok media liaison officer Hermann Coetzee said, adding that he was likely to be "a utility replacement on the bench."
Coetzee said strong-tackling Natal fly-half Henry Honiball was expected to replace van Schalkwyk at inside centre.
South Africa, who have lost their opening two Tri-Nations matches to New Zealand and Australia, will be meeting unbeaten New Zealand for the second time.
There has also been speculation that experienced wing James Small - South Africa's most capped player with 40 Springbok appearances - will come in for Russell Bennett at fullback.

Springbok coach Carel du Plessis appears to be resisting the temptation to recall World Cup fullback Andre Joubert - despite the veteran three-quarter's excellent form in recent Currie Cup games for Natal.
Coetzee said the Springbok test side would be announced later on Monday.
Coetzee also said Gauteng Lions centre Japie Mulder - travelling with the South African squad in Australasia - is still not match fit because of a shoulder injury picked up against the British Lions.
